Describe your store

Say what you sell and the features you want — for example “Today's drop”, “Only X left” badges, or a gift bundle section. The AI builds all the design from those words. You never pick colours, fonts or layout yourself.

  • Theme, colours, fonts, layout & card style

AI design — decided for you

There are no design controls here on purpose. The AI chose everything below from your description. To get a different look, change your words in the Describe tab and Generate again — you stay in charge of your name and products, the AI stays in charge of the visuals.

Theme & colours · AI chose
Pastel
Soft pastel background, rose accent, warm ink — picked for “cozy, soft, pastel”.
Fonts · AI chose
DM Serif + Karla
Heading and body pairing matched to the mood of your description.
Layout & product cards · AI chose
Grid · Soft & rounded cards
Card shape, spacing and layout follow the same mood — rounded for cozy shops, sharp for luxury ones.
Intro & headings · AI wrote
A few handmade pieces, crocheted fresh every day.
Headline, intro paragraph, section headings and story text are written by the AI — not typed by the seller.
ONToday's drop
A limited, current-only section — AI adds it when you sell a few pieces at a time.
ON“Only X left” stock badges
Live count on every card, “Sold out” at zero — AI adds it for limited stock.
OFFGift bundle section
Two favourite pieces together, ready to give. Ask for “gift bundle” in your description and the AI adds it.
ONMaker story
A warm personal section — AI adds it for handmade, personal shops.

Want a feature on or off? Just say so in your description — e.g. add “with a gift bundle section” — and Generate again. The list above and the preview update together.

Upload your own product photos — the AI looks at each photo and writes its name and description for you. No photos yet? Let the AI create sample products to start with.

No photos? No problem

Sample products match the kind of store you described, with photos, names, descriptions and prices — ready to edit in the dashboard or replace with your own.

To change any product's photo, price, name or description, open the Dashboard tab — edits update the live preview instantly.

Seller dashboard — your controls

This is everything you control manually — and it's deliberately only the basics: add or delete products, and edit each one's photo, name, price, description and quantity (stock). No colours, fonts or layout here — the AI handles all of that from your description. Set stock to 0 and the card instantly shows “Sold out”.

0Products
0Pieces in stock

DraftStore status
How stock works: the “Only X left” badge on each card comes from the stock number below. Buyers can never add more than that to the cart, and after a PayPal order is paid, the stock goes down by the amount bought — at zero the piece shows Sold out. Add or remove products whenever you like; if the store is published, hit Republish to push changes to the same link.

Store JSON

This is the exact object the preview is rendering right now. Notice the split inside it: you own store.name and every product's name, photo, price, description and stock — the AI owns theme, features, headings and intro text. Edit a product and watch only your parts change.

In the full build, a small serverless function sends the seller's prompt to an LLM (Groq / OpenAI) with a fixed schema, and this JSON is what comes back. Checkout is a second function that creates a PayPal sandbox order from the cart total and returns an approval link.

Sandbox demo — no real money moves.

How the split works here: you set the store name and every product's name, photo, price, description and quantity — nothing else. Everything visual is AI-decided from your description: theme, colours, fonts, layout, card style, intro, headings, and which sections exist (Today's drop, stock badges, gift bundles, maker story). Stock is tracked in this page — buyers can't exceed it and paid PayPal sandbox orders reduce it, flipping pieces to “Sold out” at zero. Saving stock/photos beyond this page and connecting a real PayPal sandbox app need the small serverless step; photo copy and checkout are still simulated in-browser in this demo. Generation calls the Groq AI API on the server (/api/generate) — if that call fails, a sample store is shown instead and the page says so.
